title: Lean 4 Setup Guide

canonical_node.axiom: Lean 4 verification is the authoritative check for formal structural claims in this repository.
definitions: Lean: the Lean 4 theorem prover, versioned via elan.
elan: the Lean version manager that reads lean-toolchain.
Lake: the Lean build system and project manager.
Verified: a Lean file passes when the command exits without errors.
Mathlib: the Lean mathematical library, fetched via lake exe cache get.
derivation: Lean is not installed as a single version; elan manages versions.
The repo's lean-toolchain file specifies the Lean version for elan.
Running the provided scripts or manual install sets up elan and Lean.
Verification commands (lean or lake env lean) check files without errors.
The public verification targets are TheophysicsProductionKernel.lean, CorrectedEntropyKernel.lean, and narrow_product_test/NarrowProductTest/Basic.lean.
canonical_node.action: Install Lean 4 via elan, run the verification commands on the listed files, and treat successful runs as formal verification of the structural claims.
boundary: Does not install Lean globally without elan.
Does not verify Python behavior; Python only demonstrates examples and counterexamples.
Does not guarantee Mathlib availability; slow downloads are expected.
Does not cover all possible Lean files, only the listed targets.
test: Run 'lean TheophysicsProductionKernel.lean' and 'lean CorrectedEntropyKernel.lean' and check for zero errors.
Run 'lake env lean NarrowProductTest/Basic.lean' and 'lake env lean NarrowProductTest.lean' and check for zero errors.
In VS Code, open a .lean file and confirm the Infoview shows no red errors.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Enables readers to independently verify the Lean proofs, providing a formal check of structural claims beyond Python demonstrations.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the existing Python-based demonstrations and the repository's structure; does not alter any mathematical content.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without this setup, the Lean proofs cannot be checked, and the formal verification claim collapses to unverified.

overstatement_risks: Claiming that Lean verification proves all claims in the repository, when only specific files are targeted.
Assuming that a successful Lean run implies correctness of the underlying mathematics without inspecting the proof content.
Equating Python behavior with formal verification.
kill_conditions: If the listed Lean files do not compile without errors, the verification claim fails.
If the setup instructions are incomplete or incorrect, users cannot reproduce the verification.

plain_summary: This document explains how to install Lean 4 and verify specific proof files in the repository. It is a setup guide, not a mathematical proof. The verification commands are clear, but the document does not itself establish any formal claims; it only provides the means to check them.
